needs.reason: Targets, source sets and dependencies are literal in the kotlin {} block. Only Gradle resolves kotlinx-coroutines-core to the JVM variant artifact kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm and kotlin-test to its JVM and JUnit variants.

traps: The one Gradle project has four Kotlin source sets, and dependencies are per source set: kotlinx-coroutines-core belongs to commonMain (seen by every target), slf4j-api only to jvmMain. Neither is on a configuration named implementation.
Source directories are src/<sourceSet>/kotlin, not src/main/kotlin: a reader expecting the JVM layout finds no sources.

Greeting.kt declares expect fun platformName(); its actual is in src/jvmMain/kotlin/com/example/greeting/Platform.jvm.kt. The .jvm.kt suffix is a naming convention, not a language or a target selector.

kotlinx-coroutines-core is a multiplatform coordinate: on the JVM target Gradle module metadata redirects it to org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines-core-jvm:1.9.0. The declared name stays kotlinx-coroutines-core.
jvmTest exists by convention (src/jvmTest/kotlin) although no file is there; commonTest compiles into the JVM test compilation.
kotlin("test") has no version: the plugin aligns it to 2.0.21. The Kotlin compiler and kotlin-stdlib 2.0.21 come from the plugin, not from a toolchain or a declared dependency.
